[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
{{Ireland Native}}
{{Occupation|text=was an artist and lithographer}}

'''Daniel T. Glasgow''' was born in Ireland about 1834 or 1835. He was an artist and lithographer who worked in New York before returning to Kilrea, County Londonderry, where he died in 1858.

The middle initial '''T''' is documented, but its full form has not been identified.<ref name="Heyrman">[https://drum.lib.umd.edu/bitstreams/fa470749-634c-44a5-8f50-dd4f35f08ace/download Joy Peterson Heyrman, ''"Signature Drawings": Social Networks and Collecting Practices in Antebellum Albums''], PhD dissertation, University of Maryland, 2008, pp. 151–153 and list of illustrations, p. xviii. The study identifies the Irish-born brothers James I. Glasgow, 1828–1853, and Daniel T. Glasgow, 1835–1858, and states that both worked for William Endicott & Company (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

=== Parentage ===

Daniel was described in his obituary as '''Daniel Glasgow, Jr.''' and died at Kilrea, where the elder [[Glasgow-XXXX|Daniel Glasgow]] lived.<ref name="CrayonObituary">[https://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccol/sc3500/sc3520/016800/016836/images/crayon_apr1858_1.pdf ''The Crayon''], New York, April 1858, p. 118, obituary of Daniel Glasgow, Jr., reporting that he died at Kilrea on 29 January 1858, of consumption, in the twenty-fourth year of his age (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

The elder Daniel may therefore be attached as his father.

[[Irwin-XXXX|Margaret Irwin]] is attached as Daniel's '''uncertain mother'''. Margaret and the elder Daniel were the documented parents of Robert Glasgow at Kilrea in 1827, and no other wife or mother has been identified.<ref name="RobertBaptism">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/KilreaP1/Baptisms/1827.html Richard John Torrens, "Kilrea First Presbyterian Church Records: Baptisms in 1827"], entry 146, transcribed by Barbara Braswell: Robert, son of Daniel Glasgow and Margaret Irwin of Kilrea, born 1 September and baptised 30 September 1827 (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

=== Artistic career ===

Daniel emigrated to the United States and worked for the New York lithographic firm '''William Endicott & Company'''. His older brother [[Glasgow-XXXX|James Irvin Glasgow]] worked for the same firm.<ref name="Heyrman" />

Daniel was particularly regarded as a watercolour painter. His obituary stated that, had he lived, he might have become one of the leading painters in watercolours among his circle.<ref name="CrayonObituary" />

A pencil landscape titled '''''Brook''''' is attributed to Daniel in the John Mackie Falconer Album, held by the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. The undated drawing measures approximately 3⅜ by 3¼ inches.<ref name="Heyrman" />

=== Death ===

Daniel died at Kilrea on '''29 January 1858''' from consumption, the historical term generally used for tuberculosis.<ref name="CrayonObituary" />

He was described as being '''in the twenty-fourth year of his age''', indicating that he was about twenty-three. This places his birth between approximately 30 January 1834 and 29 January 1835.

No burial record, gravestone, probate record, spouse or children have been identified.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-3896]] is assessed at 96% (proved). Daniel junior's Kilrea death, artist career and documented brotherhood with James connect him to the older Daniel whose parenthood of James is explicit. The combined sibling argument is strong even though junior alone is not a literal son clause.

Selected Glasgow-3896 fatherhood of Glasgow-3900; maternal identity and upstream ancestry are separate.

Next useful test: Compare The Crayon original with the documented artist sibling account.

Source basis already held: [https://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccol/sc3500/sc3520/016800/016836/images/crayon_apr1858_1.pdf The Crayon (https://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccol/sc 3500/sc 3520/016800/016836/images/crayon_apr1858_1.pdf), New York, April 1858, p. 118, obituary of Daniel Glasgow, Jr., reporting that he died at Kilrea on 29 January 1858, of consumption, in the twenty-fourth year of his age (accessed 16 July 2026).]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.



The dissertation gives Daniel's lifespan as 1835–1858, while the contemporary obituary places his birth in 1834 or early 1835. A birth date of '''about 1834''' or '''about 1835''' is therefore appropriate.

Margaret Irwin should remain attached as an '''uncertain''' mother because no located record explicitly names her as Daniel's mother.

The original Kilrea church registers, Daniel Glasgow senior's will and local burial records may identify Daniel's exact birth date and confirm his mother.
